mike: Quick question — finalizing rollout for `model-prefetch` flag. If org=false, project=true, route unset, model=true, which scope wins? I thought most specific wins but seen surprising fallbacks.

flags-bot: Reminder: flag `model-prefetch` exists in org+project+model scopes (lint OK) :robot_face:

sophia: Specificity order: route > model > project > org. So model=true should win if no route override. Exceptions: if any scope sets `force-off: true` or `rollout=0%` that's global.

mike: ok thanks. Two edgecases: 1) project=true but project has a canary audience limited to internal@company — does that mean model=true without matching audience will still enable? 2) If route has `audience: canaryA` but model scope has `force-off`, which holds?

anna: answers:
- (1) Scopes are evaluated first, then audience gating is applied. So model=true gives baseline enabled. If project has audience gating, that only matters for project-level toggles. If model-level is set and passes, it's enabled.
- (2) `force-off` wins over any enables at less specific scopes. So route audience can't turn it on if model has `force-off`.

sophia: short pseudo example:
```
org: { enabled: false }
project: { enabled: true, audience: "internal" }
model: { enabled: true }
route: {}  // unset
=> result: enabled (model scope)
```
and
```
model: { force_off: true }
route: { enabled: true, audience: "canaryA" }
=> result: disabled (force_off wins)
```

lucas: I'll add a unit test for the inheritance matrix and a diag log to make resolution visible in traces. cc @mike

mike: awesome — can you also add a small note in ops-runbook about the 'audience evaluated after scope chosen' rule? helps oncall. :pray:

lucas: yup, PR incoming today.

sophia: also adding a lint to warn when project audience exists but model explicitly enables — can cause surprises.

mike: thanks all :+1:
